Subject: Post-call: RTBF / Deletion expectations & next steps

Hi Alice / Rajesh —

Thanks again for the chat today. Quick recap and the agreed next steps so we have everything in one place:

What we covered
- RTBF (right to be forgotten) workflow overview for FinTechCo users and API customers.
- Data residency: primary production data for your account is stored in us-east-1; EU residency is possible for European sub-accounts (we discussed later follow-up if you want EU-only).
- Logging & audit: access logs kept for 90 days by default; we can extend on request.

Action items / timelines (as discussed)
1) Deletion from active stores: we can remove PII from primary DBs within 48 hours of a validated request.
2) Caches & KV: prefixes and KV caches are invalidated within minutes and fully purged as part of the deletion job.
3) Backups & snapshots: backups are retained for the configured retention window (default 90 days). Purging a record from backups is tied to snapshot lifecycle and generally completes within 30–90 days depending on snapshot timing.
4) Logs & audit: audit events referencing the deletion will remain; we can redact user-identifying fields on request but maintain an audit trail of the deletion event.
5) Expedited purge: we can offer an expedited backup purge (out-of-cycle restore/redact/snapshot) for an additional services fee.

Next steps we agreed on
- Please confirm whether FinTechCo requires an expedited purge option or whether the standard snapshot-based window is acceptable.
- Send the formal deletion request via the portal or reply to this thread with the user identifiers and any legal hold information.
- I’m looping in Dev (cc) and Legal for details on backup constraints and any contractual language we should prepare.

Attachments: RTBF_Process.pdf (high-level flow), backup-retention-2026.xlsx (backup schedule by region)

Thanks — happy to hop on another quick call if useful.

Hi Alice —

Answering your questions inline below and adding technical/contract notes from our side.

1) Backups:
- Primary backups are object-store snapshots (S3 standard) in the same region as production. We do not proactively move customer snapshots to Glacier in our default config; cold-tiering is only done when customers request long-term archival.
- For standard retention (90 days), purge from backups occurs on the next snapshot rotation that removes the snapshot containing the records. That means the effective purge timeframe is tied to the time since the last snapshot that included the data — hence the 30–90 day window.
- If you need permanent purge faster, we offer an expedited process: we can restore the snapshot to a private cluster, run a targeted redact/purge for the identifiers, take a new snapshot, and delete the old snapshot. This process typically takes 3–10 business days and is considered a billable professional-services workflow.

2) Logs & redaction:
- Our default is to retain structured access logs (timestamp, request id, route) for 90 days. PII fields are not stored in plaintext in those logs for production customers unless explicitly enabled.
- Redaction is configurable: we can run a redaction of stored logs for specific user identifiers, but this is an intrusive operation and requires legal sign-off. Redaction will preserve forensic metadata (timestamps, request ids) but remove or pseudonymize user-identifying fields.

3) Attestation:
- We can provide a signed deletion attestation once the deletion pipeline has completed for the provided identifiers. The attestation includes: deletion timestamp for the active store, confirmation of cache invalidation, and a statement of backup purge timing (and whether expedited purge was performed).

I’ve attached the RTBF_Process.pdf and the backup schedule spreadsheet for region-specific snapshot cadence.

Dev — can you confirm the typical snapshot cadence for FinTechCo’s account in us-east-1 and the expected worst-case time to complete an expedited purge?

Laura — could you confirm any standard contract language we should surface (DPA addendum / expedited purge terms)?

Thanks,
Camila

Subject: Re: Post-call: RTBF / Deletion expectations & next steps

Hi all — quick technical note from infra:

- Snapshot cadence for FinTechCo (us-east-1): incremental snapshots every 24 hours, full snapshot weekly. Retention policy is 90 days by default (configurable).
- Worst-case standard purge window: if the deleted record was captured in the weekly full snapshot immediately after deletion, it could remain in backups until that snapshot ages out (up to ~90 days).
- Expedited purge flow (3–10 business days typical):
  1) Create a private restore of the snapshot that contains the data.
  2) Run a targeted purge job to delete/redact the identifiers.
  3) Create a new snapshot from the cleansed data.
  4) Delete the original snapshot(s).
- We can provide hashes and a signed log of the purge operation for attestation.
- Important caveat: if there is a legal hold (litigation or regulatory), we cannot purge until the hold is lifted. Please indicate holds in the deletion request.

If you want, we can schedule the restore/redact job as soon as we receive the deletion request and signed authorization. Note that the restore requires short-term dedicated capacity and a change-control ticket (we’ll do this in a maintenance window to avoid customer impact).

Hi Alice —

A few legal points to confirm so we can proceed with the attestation and, if requested, an expedited purge:

1) Legal hold: please confirm whether any regulatory or litigation hold applies to the accounts/identifiers in scope. If a hold exists, deletion will be paused until we receive written confirmation from FinTechCo releasing the hold.

2) DPA / contractual terms: our standard DPA covers data deletion obligations and backup retention language. For expedited purge services, we require a signed addendum that outlines the scope of work and associated fees. I can draft a short addendum and send it via DocuSign as soon as you confirm the scope.

3) Attestation: once the deletion (and any expedited purge) is complete, we will provide a signed attestation that includes: timestamped confirmation of active-store deletion, cache invalidation confirmation, and a statement of backup purge action or schedule. For expedited purges we will also include operation hashes and the engineer responsible for the restore/redact job.

Please reply with: (a) confirmation on holds, (b) whether you want to proceed with standard snapshot purge or expedited purge for the initial 3 accounts, and (c) whether you want the DPA addendum sent now.

Thanks — I’ll stage a DocuSign for the addendum if you want it routed.
